definition: An assessment of the risks that arise from using the reviewed methods, such as misuse, dual use, or unsupported assurance, as distinct from the threats those methods address and from lists of open technical challenges. Y: a dedicated analysis with mitigations. P: an explicit but limited treatment. N: none.
method: Full text converted to plain text and searched, body only (reference lists excluded), for dual-use, misuse, ethics, responsible disclosure, malicious use and risk, and for section headings on ethics, risks, limitations and challenges. Every hit was read in context. Two reviews were read in the browser on the publisher pages. Checked on 2026-11-17.

reviews.evidence: No passage assesses risks that arise from using red-teaming methods. 'Dual-use' has no hit in the body and 'misuse' appears only as the topic of a benchmark. There is no ethics or responsible-disclosure section. Section 3 is a taxonomy of the risks that red teaming looks for, and Section 9 lists future directions.

reviews.version: version of record, Information Processing and Management 62 (2025) 104239, 48 pages
reviews.evidence: No passage assesses risks that arise from using red-teaming methods. 'Dual-use' and 'responsible disclosure' have no hit. 'Misuse' and 'ethical' refer to the misuse and deployment of LLMs, which red teaming is meant to expose. Section 6.2 calls for more attention to the ethical implications of deploying LLMs, and Section 7.3, the impact statement, discusses the review's contribution and the limits of automated evaluation.

Section 10.4, 'Ethical Considerations and Responsible Disclosure', states that a catalog of attacks "has dual-use implications" and describes two choices made to limit them. Section 9 covers limitations and threats to validity. Partial because the risk treated is that of the survey itself; there is no analysis of risks by method and no mitigation per risk.

Section V, 'Challenges and Limitations', lists technical challenges (encoding, trainability, hardware, algorithmic maturity, integration). Section V.F treats one security risk, the threat that quantum computers pose to the cryptography protecting LLM systems (harvest now, decrypt later). No hit for dual-use, misuse or ethics; prompt injection is mentioned once. Partial because the risk treated comes from quantum computing in general, not from using the reviewed methods.
